text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000169 bills 99215 at about three times the complexity-adjusted expectation, and its returned charts support the billed levels, but heavy note duplication leaves open whether that documentation reflects the actual visits.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The excess is not explained by a sicker panel: the 99215 share is roughly double the all-provider rate in every complexity band, including 0–1 condition patients. Sampled examples include single-diagnosis visits such as C0096163 and C0096213 (N39.0) and C0096299 (R21), and 99214 also dominates the overall mix. Against that, all 17 documented 99215 claims were supported at high MDM. The usual all-provider unsupported rate is 15%, so a 0% rate would normally point toward a legitimately complex practice. That reassurance is weakened because records cover only about 2% of claims and 49% of returned notes were flagged as duplicates, with a 13% repeated-time rate. This suggests possible templated or cloned notes that would match the billed level regardless of what happened, and the 4 moderate-plus data notes without a lab line point the same way, though weakly. A reviewer should first compare the duplicate-flagged notes side by side and request the EHR audit trail, which was not received. They should then pull charts for the low-complexity 99215 claims listed in the packet to see whether the documented MDM is specific to each encounter."}
